items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 Multiplayer Finally Goes Live From Screen Rant (Written by Tom Wilson) on November 16, 2026 | OpenCritic

Cyberpunk 2077 is the game that keeps on growing. CD Projekt Red, six years after the base game dropped, has released numerous updates of varying significance, as well as the critically acclaimed expansion and assorted expanded media releases. There is simply no shortage of ways to interact with Night City and the wider Cyberpunk world, unless you want to do so with a friend, of course. Cyberpunk 2077's official multiplayer was canceled back in 2021, with CD Projekt Red stating there are no plans to implement it in the future.

Naturally, this proved to be a huge blow to the game's fanbase, who had dreamed of roaming through Night City with their friends. However, it also proved to be a challenge for modders, who have since set about implementing what CD Projekt Red lacked the resources and time for. We've gotten announcements of a Far Cry -esque Cyberpunk 2077 co-op mod that makes the entire game's story playable with a friend, as well as a full-blown multiplayer experience which has finally gone live.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 PC players can finally become Night City heroes in original expansion mod
items.summary: Make a difference in Night City 🚑
items.content:
This Cyberpunk 2077 PC mod lets you join one of Night City's most-famous emergency response teams.

In another lifetime, Cyberpunk 2077 could have been the biggest release of the decade, even surpassing Grand Theft Auto VI , had it launched in the intended way.

Over the years though, it’s become the game it was always meant to be, and official mod support on PC, PlayStation and Xbox platforms make it even better.

If you want to make a real difference in Night City, drop the cyberware upgrades, forget the bounty hunting, and join the Trauma Team through this awesome in-progress expansion mod.

Going a step beyond what you’d typically expect of a questline mod, Join Trauma Team - AV Rescue Shifts introduces a fully-voiced team of characters who you’ll join on dangerous retrieval missions.

You’ll no doubt have seen the Night City Trauma Team in action. When someone’s hurt, and can afford the service, they’ll descend from the sky in an armoured vehicle, fend off attackers, and get the victim to safety. Now you get to join them.

The mod’s description says you’ll get an in-game text message asking if you want to join. You then “go to the interview at the Medical Center in Little China, and they put you on probation".

"Then you take the staff elevator to the roof, get changed in the armory, meet your crew and board the AV.”

At the time of writing, there’s only one shift available, but you can repeat it as many times as you want. The AV will transport you to the scene of the crime and once you take down the enemies and retrieve your client you’ll be paid for your troubles.

It’s the kind of side-activity that we’d have loved to see in the full-game as while Night City is gorgeous, there’s very little to do in terms of open-world interactivity.

After taking the Join Trauma Team mod for a spin myself, I can confidently say it’s great, and I’m hoping more missions are added soon.

Weirdly though, it reminded me most of my time with Grand Theft Auto IV … One of my favourite parts of the game was hijacking a police cruiser and using its radio to track down criminals at large, and it was disappointing to see it absent from Grand Theft Auto V .

Given the hype around GTA VI’s open-world, this is the exact type of content I’d love to see return in Leonida, and I think Cyberpunk 2 should consider it too.

Public service vehicles like police cars, ambulances, taxis should all come with unique functionality. It makes the world feel more alive and does wonders for keeping the overall gameplay experience fresh.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Lands on Battle.net at $17.99 Intro Price
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 Battle.net launched Nov. 10 with a $17.99 intro price that ends Nov. 16. See prices, the Edgerunners 2 update and what Blizzard says.
items.content:
Image: CD PROJEKT RED Cyberpunk 2077 went on sale in Blizzard’s Battle.net shop on November 10, 2026, and the launch pricing runs out today. According to TalkEsport , the US introductory prices were $17.99 for the base game and $31.99 for the Ultimate Edition, with a stated end date of November 16 and higher prices after that.

What Blizzard and CD PROJEKT RED Launched on November 10 Battle.net Prices: $17.99, $31.99 and the November 16 Deadline What the Edgerunners 2 Update Adds on Battle.net Graphics options and upscaling changes Content, tours and mods How the Battle.net Deal Came Together Why Blizzard Says It Is Not Chasing Steam or Epic Battle.net vs Steam, Epic and GOG: Where the Fourth Storefront Fits Is Battle.net really the fourth store? Market Impact for CD PROJEKT RED: 40 Million Copies and a New Channel Blizzard’s Fall Calendar: WoW Forever, Hearthstone and Now Cyberpunk Launch Problems: Download and Install Reports on Blizzard’s Forums What PC Players Should Do Before the Price Rises The Witcher 3 Pipeline and What Else Could Follow Cyberpunk Historical Context: From a Blizzard-Only Launcher to a Multi-Publisher Shop Five Predictions for Battle.net After Cyberpunk 2077 What Remains Unconfirmed About the Battle.net Launch FAQ: Cyberpunk 2077 on Battle.net Related Coverage Three products arrived together: Cyberpunk 2077, the Phantom Liberty expansion, and Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition, which bundles the two. Every Battle.net version includes the free Edgerunners 2 Update. Coverage calls Battle.net the fourth PC storefront for the game after Steam, GOG and the Epic Games Store, a label that works better as a market description than an official designation.

The launch matters beyond one discount. Battle.net spent years as the home of Blizzard and Activision releases, and a CD PROJEKT RED flagship is its clearest step toward carrying outside publishers. Anyone adding another launcher to a PC also adds another account to protect, which is why a short guide to securing gaming accounts is worth a read before you sign in.

The week's biggest stories in tech, gaming and security, in one email.

Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.

The release was announced as a partnership between CD PROJEKT RED and Blizzard Entertainment. Blizzard’s own news post, dated November 10, describes the game as out now on Battle.net, and GamerHeadlines reported the same launch the following day. Players can buy the base game, the Phantom Liberty expansion on its own, or the Ultimate Edition that holds both.

One detail trips up shoppers. CD PROJEKT RED’s own pages state that Cyberpunk 2077 is required to play Phantom Liberty, so the expansion is not a standalone purchase in practice. Blizzard’s announcement does not say the expansion comes free with the base game either. If you want both, the Ultimate Edition is the single-click route.

The Battle.net arrival also makes a recent official list out of date. The studio’s Update 2.5 posts from late October named Steam, GOG and the Epic Games Store for PC and Mac, with no mention of Battle.net. That roster no longer matches what a PC shopper sees today.

The game itself is a long-running seller. CD PROJEKT RED has said Cyberpunk 2077 passed 40 million copies sold, and that Phantom Liberty sold 15 million copies in less than three years. A fresh storefront does not change the game, but it does put an established title in front of a different audience at a launch discount.

The reported US launch prices are $17.99 for Cyberpunk 2077 and $31.99 for the Ultimate Edition. Battle.net’s storefront banner advertises savings of up to 70% with an introductory discount. The offer is stated to end on November 16, after which prices will rise. Blizzard’s launch announcement confirms availability but does not publish a price, so the dollar figures come from launch coverage rather than from Blizzard itself.

A little arithmetic shows what the bundle is worth. The Ultimate Edition costs $14 more than the base game at the reported prices, which puts the implied cost of Phantom Liberty inside the bundle at $14. That reading is an inference from two launch prices, not a figure Blizzard published.

For buyers, the practical rule is simple. If the plan is to own both halves of the game on Battle.net, the bundle at $31.99 beats buying pieces. After today, check the live price before assuming any of these numbers still apply, since Blizzard said they will go up.

The Battle.net build ships with Update 2.5, branded the Edgerunners 2 Update. CD PROJEKT RED announced the update alongside the Netflix premiere of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, and it reached the game’s other platforms on October 22. Battle.net buyers get the same content on day one, with no separate charge.

Check out what's coming to Cyberpunk 2077 in the Edgerunners 2 Update!
items.summary: Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you! Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watc
items.content:
Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you!

Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watch the Features Overview video to see some of the new features in action:

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

items.title: Patch 2.31
items.summary: Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live! This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below: Vehicles Updated Aut
items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]
